title: The Tortoise and the Hare
source: Aesop's Fables (public domain), gently retold for bedtime

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Once upon a time, in a green and sunny meadow, there lived a hare who was very, very fast.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He could zip through the clover, and leap over the logs, and race the wind itself.

lines.speaker: hare
lines.text: Whee! Nobody is faster than me! Nobody in the whole wide world!
lines.speech: [excited] Whee! Nobody is faster than me! Nobody in the whole wide world!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the same meadow lived a tortoise. He was not fast at all. He walked slowly, and carefully, one little step at a time.

lines.speaker: hare
lines.text: Ha! Good morning, Tortoise! Are you going somewhere? Because at that speed, you'll get there next week!
lines.speech: [laughs] Ha! Good morning, Tortoise! [teasing] Are you going somewhere? Because at that speed, you'll get there next week!

lines.speaker: tortoise
lines.text: Good morning, Hare. I may be slow... but I always get where I am going.
lines.speech: [warmly] Good morning, Hare. [chuckles softly] I may be slow... but I always get where I am going.

lines.speaker: tortoise
lines.text: Shall we have a race, you and I? From the old oak stump, all the way to the big willow tree by the pond.
lines.speech: [thoughtful] Shall we have a race, you and I? From the old oak stump, all the way to the big willow tree by the pond.

lines.speaker: hare
lines.text: A race? With you? Oh, ho, ho! Alright, Tortoise. This will be easy!
lines.speech: [surprised] A race? With you? [laughs] Oh, ho, ho! [confident] Alright, Tortoise. This will be easy!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The next morning, the little birds of the meadow came to watch. And so did the wise old owl.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The wise old owl lifted her wing. On your marks... get set... go!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Whoosh! The hare shot off like an arrow, and in the blink of an eye, he was far, far away.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the tortoise? He took one slow step. And then another. And then another.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Halfway to the willow tree, the hare stopped and looked back. The tortoise was nowhere to be seen.

lines.speaker: hare
lines.text: Hmm. That slowpoke is miles behind me. I have plenty of time for a little nap.
lines.speech: [smug] Hmm. That slowpoke is miles behind me. [yawns] I have plenty of time for a little nap.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the hare lay down in the cool shade of a hawthorn bush. The sun was warm, the bees were humming, and soon... he was fast asleep.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Meanwhile, the tortoise kept on walking. Step, by step, by step. He didn't stop, and he didn't hurry. He just kept going.

lines.speaker: tortoise
lines.text: Slow and steady. Slow and steady. One more step, and then one more.
lines.speech: [softly, determined] Slow and steady. Slow and steady. One more step, and then one more.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He walked past the daisies. He walked past the stream. And then, very quietly, he walked right past the sleeping hare.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When the hare finally woke up, the sun was sinking low. He rubbed his eyes, and looked toward the willow tree, and...

lines.speaker: hare
lines.text: Oh no! The tortoise! He's almost there!
lines.speech: [panicked] Oh no! The tortoise! He's almost there!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The hare ran as fast as he could. Faster than ever before! But it was too late.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: With one last slow and steady step, the tortoise crossed the finish line under the big willow tree. And all the animals cheered!

lines.speaker: hare
lines.text: You won, Tortoise. I was so sure I would win, that I didn't even try.
lines.speech: [sheepish] You won, Tortoise. [sincere] I was so sure I would win, that I didn't even try.

lines.speaker: tortoise
lines.text: That's alright, Hare. Being fast is a wonderful thing. But slow and steady can get you there too.
lines.speech: [kindly] That's alright, Hare. Being fast is a wonderful thing. But slow and steady can get you there too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And so, the hare learned that it doesn't matter how fast you are. What matters is that you keep going, and never give up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That evening, the two new friends sat by the pond, under the willow tree, and watched the fireflies come out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The hare curled up in the soft grass. The tortoise tucked his head into his cosy shell.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The stars came out, one by one. The meadow was quiet. And it was time for everyone to rest.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Goodnight, little one. Sweet dreams.
